main_text.p: ter hos erant quoq; ἀσυνόμοι, qui mun-diciem & decoré urbis, ὁδοποιοί qui vias intra extraq; urbem, ἐπισκέπτ[?]ὴ τ̀ ὑδά-των, qui aquarum inductionem in urbe, κρηνοφύλακες[?], qui fontium custodiam sibi commissam habebant: quorum omnium curatione Aristoteles uno nomine ἀσυνομίαν[?] appellat. Quo pertinuere etiam ἐπιμελητ̀ τ̀ δημοσίων ἔργων[?], qui opera & aedificia publica ad urbis magnificentiam facientia struebat: munus extraordinarium, curationis potius quàm magistratus nomine afficiendū, quo magnificè ac sumptuosè defunctus fuit Pericles: [illegible, ~3 letters]Ujus rationes ne reddere cogeretur, suggerente Alcibiade adolescéte putatur [illegible, ~2 letters]suafu suo civitate difficili bello Peloponnesiaco implicuisse, ut hujus cura à curâ reposcendarū rationū eam abstraheret.

Huic persimilis curatio fuit & τειχοποιΐα[?], curatores τειχοποιοί[?] à muris extruendis aut reficiédis sic nuncupati, deni numero, finguli nimirū, cū posceret usus, à qualibet tribu editi, cujusmodi τειχοποιός[?] à tribu suâ Pandionià creatus fuit Orator [illegible, ~2 letters]Demosthenes: unde orta causa illa nobile coronâ Demosthenis decretâ à Ctesiphonte, accusante ob decretū hoc Ctesiphonte Æschine, defendente Demosth.

page.notes: Greek words are transcribed as far as legible; accents and several letters of the Greek words (ἐπισκέπτ[?]ὴ, κρηνοφύλακες, ἀσυνομίαν, ἐπιμελητ̀, τειχοποιΐα, τειχοποιοί, τειχοποιός) are doubtful and marked [?]. The left-margin notes are small, cut or overprinted and cannot be read; they are shown as illegible. Notes at the foot of the page, lower left, are also illegible. The initial of "Ujus" is blurred. "Pandionià" and "Æschine" are copied as printed. The line "honté Æschine" has the Ctesiphonte name printed as "honte" after a hyphen, reconstructed from the line above.
